lead: The assistant already chats, remembers, and has safeguards. Continuous operation is optional: on Linux, a service can start the bot when you log in. Finish by reviewing the safeguards and choosing only the next step you’ll use.
objetivo: Check memory, audit, and safeguards; if you use Telegram on Linux, set up the user service.

aprende.t: Separate what’s been tested from what still needs testing

hero_alt: A shop owner checks a simple list beside a realistic humanoid assistant before turning it on.

secoes.sub: The path ends with a check, not a magic button.

nos.detalhe: Review identity files and look up a real fact in the database.
Keep the approval policy appropriate and read the command history.
Use the box runner when you want to limit the reach of commands.
Use caixa.sh when Codex or Claude Code works on your project code.
systemd is Linux’s service manager. The user service file starts the bot; adjust the paths before enabling it.

secoes.legenda: Click each part to see what it does.

secoes.sub: Click each step to see what to do.

texto: The command checks installation, database, configuration, and secrets required by the active options.
“Done” in the reply isn’t a receipt. auditoria -n 20 prints JSON lines: comando is the request, classe is free/approve/blocked, rodou says whether it ran, and decisao explains why.
The example service uses systemd, Linux’s service manager, to start Telegram. journalctl shows that service’s logs. If you only use the terminal, you don’t need to install it.

Local Ollama, Linux, and the command runner box with Docker were tested live. OpenRouter, live Telegram, and macOS were not tested live by INEMA. Windows was tested only through WSL with Ubuntu, also without a live test.

secoes.sub: WorkingDirectory and ExecStart are the folder and command the service runs. Check these paths in the file before copying; the example assumes the clone is in ~/intelecto-v2.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/intelecto-v2
python3 -m intelecto verificar
python3 -m intelecto memoria
python3 -m intelecto auditoria -n 20

cd ~/intelecto-v2
cat servico/intelecto-telegram.service
# Check WorkingDirectory and ExecStart; adjust if needed.
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp servico/intelecto-telegram.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now intelecto-telegram

abas.html:
{"ts": "2026-11-13T03:38:00+00:00", "tipo": "comando", "comando": "ls", "classe": "livre", "rodou": true, "decisao": "livre (só leitura)"}

In this line, comando is ls, classe is livre, rodou is true, and decisao explains why it was allowed.

secoes.sub: Follow the steps in order and check each one only after you’ve confirmed the result.

exercicios.texto: Run the three status commands and note which fact memory found and which command the audit records.
exercicios.pronto: verificar ends with “tudo certo”; if you’ve already used memory and commands, the lines match what you did. The history can also be empty before the first command.

exercicios.texto: If you program with agents, use caixa-do-agente in a project. If you use Telegram on Linux, adjust the service file before enabling it.
exercicios.pronto: You know which layer you activated and what concrete proof confirms it works.

secoes.sub: Choose before opening the explanation. If you get it wrong, use the link to review.

perguntas.p: When does the Linux service make sense?
opcoes: When you use only the offline demo
When you want the Telegram bot active in the session
perguntas.explica: The example service starts Telegram; the terminal alone doesn’t require a service.

perguntas.p: What shows whether a command actually ran?
perguntas.explica: The audit records the command, class, decision, and whether it ran.

perguntas.p: Which item has no live test from INEMA?
perguntas.explica: Telegram was tested against a fake server, but not live; Ollama and the box had real-world proof.

itens.texto: Identity, approval, history, and boxes are visible choices.
Use the specific tool’s guide when you need to configure service or integration details.
